provenance.correctness_note: scripts/forge_driver.py gates the FlyDSL port against the live Triton output. scripts/task_runner.py validates whichever implementation is under test against an independent float64 golden transcribed from fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode_kernel (fused_recurrent.py:504-533) -- a strictly stronger oracle, because it also catches a bug the port would inherit by imitating the source. raw_beta is passed PRE-sigmoid because both kernels apply sigmoid internally (fused_recurrent.py:525, chunk.py:470). Gate uses the safe-gate branch selected by gate_lower_bound=-5.0. Both kernels update the state in place, so the golden snapshots the starting state before the kernel runs.

kda_config.source: K3 config.json linear_attn_config, recorded verbatim in the session specialist logs
kda_config.gate_note: gate_lower_bound is not a clamp: a non-null value selects the safe-gate branch gate = lower_bound * sigmoid(exp(A_log) * (raw_g + dt_bias)) instead of the softplus branch gate = -exp(A_log) * softplus(raw_g + dt_bias) used when it is null (fused_recurrent.py:513-521, chunk.py:507-515).

rewrite_contract.signature: build_kda_linear_attn_module(num_heads, head_dim, chunk_size) -> launch_fn(out, q, k, v, raw_g, raw_beta, A_log, dt_bias, state, state_indices, cu_seqlens, scale, lower_bound)
rewrite_contract.one_entry_note: The source exposes two entries -- fused_recurrent_kda_packed_decode for the packed_decode case and chunk_kda_with_fused_gate for the chunk cases -- but they evaluate the SAME gated delta-rule recurrence, one token-serial and one blockwise. The port therefore implements a single varlen entry parameterised by cu_seqlens and state_indices, and decode is the degenerate case of one token per segment. --ref-bench-mode still times the two real Triton entries with their native signatures, so the speedup baseline is the framework's actual code path.

tensors.out: [T, H, D] bf16, written in place
tensors.q, k, v: [T, H, D] bf16. Row stride is NOT assumed to be H*D: in the decode case these are strided views into the packed mixed_qkv block, so the row stride is 3*H*D. Read the tensor strides.
tensors.state: [S, H, D, D] fp32 laid out [slot, head, v, k], updated IN PLACE
tensors.state_indices: [N] int32, the state slot of each segment
tensors.scale: python float, D ** -0.5, applied to the l2-normalised q
tensors.lower_bound: python float, -5.0, selects the safe-gate branch

rewrite_contract.semantics: For each segment n, S = state[state_indices[n]] and t running over [cu_seqlens[n], cu_seqlens[n+1]): g = lower_bound * sigmoid(exp(A_log)[h] * (raw_g[t,h,:] + dt_bias[h,:])); qn = l2norm(q[t]) * scale; kn = l2norm(k[t]) with l2norm(x) = x / sqrt(sum(x^2) + 1e-6); S *= exp(g) broadcast over the v axis; vt = v[t] - (S * kn).sum(-1); vt *= sigmoid(raw_beta[t]); S += outer(vt, kn); out[t] = (S * qn).sum(-1). S stays in fp32. chunk_size is the blocking hint the source uses (64); the recurrence is exact for any blocking, so it constrains performance, not semantics.
